title: KOMPARASI TERM FREQUENCY–INVERSE DOCUMENT FREQUENCY (TF-IDF) DAN INDOBERT EMBEDDING PADA REGRESI LOGISTIK UNTUK ANALISIS SENTIMEN (Studi Kasus: Isu Feminisme)
abstract: Perkembangan media sosial telah menjadikan platform X sebagai ruang utama bagi masyarakat untuk menyampaikan opini terhadap berbagai isu sosial, termasuk feminisme. Analisis sentimen menjadi salah satu pendekatan yang dapat digunakan untuk mengidentifikasi kecenderungan opini tersebut secara otomatis. Keberhasilan analisis sentimen sangat dipengaruhi oleh metode representasi teks yang digunakan sebelum proses klasifikasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan membandingkan performa representasi teks berbasis Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) dan IndoBERT embedding pada algoritma regresi logistik dalam klasifikasi sentimen isu feminisme pada data X berbahasa Indonesia. Data penelitian berupa 4.508 tweet yang dikumpulkan melalui web scraping menggunakan 16 kata kunci terkait feminisme selama periode Januari–Desember 2025. Setelah tahap praproses, tweet kemudian dilabeli menggunakan pendekatan semi-supervised learning melalui metode pseudo-labeling. Sebagian tweet dilabeli secara manual untuk finetuning model IndoBERT sebagai teacher model, sedangkan data sisanya diberi label secara otomatis menggunakan ambang kepercayaan 0,8. Setelah eliminasi data berlabel netral, diperoleh dataset akhir sebanyak 1.196 tweet. Evaluasi dilakukan menggunakan stratified k-fold cross validation dengan metrik akurasi, presisi, recall, dan F1-score. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi TFIDF dan regresi logistik memperoleh akurasi 94,40%, presisi 97,52%, recall 95,33%, dan F1-score 96,40%. Sementara itu, kombinasi IndoBERT embedding dan regresi logistik menghasilkan akurasi 95,40%, presisi 97,08%, recall 97,13%, dan F1-score 97,09%. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa IndoBERT embedding memberikan performa yang lebih baik pada sebagian besar metrik evaluasi, sedangkan TF-IDF hanya sedikit lebih unggul pada metrik presisi. Dengan demikian, representasi berbasis konteks semantik melalui IndoBERT embedding lebih efektif dibandingkan representasi berbasis frekuensi kata untuk klasifikasi sentimen isu feminisme pada data X menggunakan algoritma regresi logistik. The widespread use of social media has made X a primary platform for people to express opinions on various social issues, including feminism. Sentiment analysis provides an effective approach for automatically identifying these opinions. The performance of sentiment analysis is highly influenced by the text representation method used prior to classification. This study aims to compare the performance of Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) and IndoBERT embeddings as text representation methods for logistic regression in sentiment classification of Indonesian-language posts related to feminism on X. The dataset consisted of 4,508 tweets collected through web scraping using 16 feminism-related keywords during the period of January to December 2025. After preprocessing, the tweets were labeled using a semi-supervised learning approach through pseudolabeling. A subset of the tweets was manually annotated to fine-tune an IndoBERT model as the teacher model, while the remaining tweets were labeled automatically using a confidence threshold of 0.8. After removing neutral instances, the final dataset contained 1,196 tweets. Model performance was evaluated using Stratified K-Fold Cross Validation with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score as evaluation metrics. The results show that the TF-IDF and logistic regression model achieved an accuracy of 94.40%, precision of 97.52%, recall of 95.33%, and an F1-score of 96.40%. Meanwhile, the IndoBERT embedding and logistic regression model achieved an accuracy of 95.40%, precision of 97.08%, recall of 97.13%, and an F1-score of 97.09%. These findings indicate that IndoBERT embeddings outperformed TF-IDF on most evaluation metrics, while TF-IDF achieved a slightly higher precision. Therefore, contextual semantic representations provided by IndoBERT embeddings are more effective than frequency-based representations for sentiment classification of feminism-related discussions on X using logistic regression.

title: Using Interaction Log Data to Evaluate and Improve Feedback Accuracy in an ILTS
abstract: This project contains an extract of interaction log data used in the analysis and evaluation described in the paper "Using Interaction Log Data to Evaluate and Improve Feedback Accuracy in an ILTS" by Soliar et al. (2026, in press). The data originates from two randomized controll studies conducted using an intelligent language tutoring system "FeedBook" (https://feedbook.website/). title: Bucket Aggregation in Bucket-Based Priority Queues for Heuristic Search
abstract: Bucket-based priority queues can reduce the overhead of priority queue operations for A* and related bounded-suboptimal and anytime variants, especially when transition costs are small integers. The buckets are usually indexed by both f-cost (primary) and h-cost (secondary), which enables efficient tie-breaking and priority ordering. However, when solution costs are large and the heuristic is informative, the number of secondary buckets within a primary bucket can become very large, leading to bucket sparsity that degrades performance. To address this, we introduce a simple aggregation method that restores bucket density while preserving standard solution-quality guarantees. We demonstrate its effectiveness in several benchmark domains.

title: Federated learning-enhanced digital twin for intelligent warehouse management and demand forecasting
abstract: Modern warehouse management faces escalating challenges in demand volatility, data privacy constraints across distributed facilities, and the need for real-time operational optimization. Traditional centralized forecasting approaches require pooling sensitive inventory data from geographically dispersed warehouses, raising significant privacy and regulatory concerns. This paper proposes FL-DT-WM, a Federated Learning-Enhanced Digital Twin framework for intelligent warehouse management and demand forecasting. The framework integrates federated learning algorithms (FedAvg and FedProx) with digital twin simulation to enable collaborative model training across distributed warehouses without sharing raw data. A Transformer-based demand forecasting module captures long-range temporal dependencies in sales patterns, while a GRU-based inventory optimizer dynamically adjusts stock levels based on digital twin simulations. We evaluate FL-DT-WM on three datasets: Kaggle Walmart Sales, UCI Online Retail, and a custom multi-warehouse dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that FL-DT-WM achieves MAE reductions of 8.3-14.7% over centralized and local baselines, improves warehouse space utilization by 12.5-19.8%, and reduces inventory holding costs by 10.2-15.6%. Comprehensive comparisons against ARIMA, Prophet, centralized LSTM, local LSTM, FedAvg-MLP, and DeepAR confirm the superiority of the proposed approach across multiple performance dimensions.

title: Reinforcement Learning and Model-based Planning in Practice: A Survey of Algorithmic Rationale and Domain Applications
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is a foundational framework in Artificial Intelligence (AI) that enables agents to acquire optimal decision-making strategies through interactions with their environments. Building on principles of trial-and-error learning, RL adapts dynamically by leveraging feedback in the form of rewards or penalties. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of RL, its integration with Deep Learning into Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), and the emerging field of model-based planning. It systematically examines a wide range of algorithms, from classical tabular methods to state-of-the-art DRL techniques, while evaluating their scalability, sample efficiency, and applicability in various domains. The survey offers an in-depth analysis of the strengths and limitations of these approaches, along with practical guidance for selecting and implementing RL algorithms. Key challenges, such as convergence, stability, and the exploration-exploitation trade-off, are thoroughly addressed to tackle real-world constraints. Additionally, this work explores the transformative impact of RL across diverse fields, including robotics, autonomous systems, intelligent transportation, energy management, and financial modeling. By bridging theoretical advancements and practical applications, this survey aims to provide researchers and practitioners with a comprehensive understanding of RL’s capabilities for solving complex and dynamic problems in AI and beyond.

title: p-Spin Glass Network Efficient Single-Batch Continual Learning
abstract: Modern sequence models heavily rely on massive memory footprints and large-batch stochastic optimization, barriers that restrict sample efficiency and continual learning. We introduce the $p$-Spin Glass Network, a novel architecture that overcomes these limitations, structurally manages optimization variance and yields four noticeable capabilities: 1. It enforces memory efficiency: native ternary quantization compresses internal parameters by $8\times$, while exact implicit gradients strictly bound activation memory to $\mathcal{O}(B \cdot T \cdot D)$. 2. it demonstrates sample efficiency, matching the asymptotic performance of a Transformer baseline while utilizing $8\times$ fewer training sequences. 3. Method enables single-batch stability and smooth, monotonic convergence at a stochastic micro-batch size of $1$. 4. Finally, this stability proves modality-agnostic, maintaining robust temporal credit assignment across both discrete subword and long horizon uncompressed raw byte streams. Ultimately, this work removes large batch requirement for stable deep learning, establishing a foundation for continuous learning and edge AI.

title: Can Language Models Understand mmWave Data? Benchmarking Large Language Models for mmWave Radar-Based Human Understanding
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown remarkable reasoning and generative capabilities, motivating their use as universal reasoning engines for perception. While modern approaches such as vision-language models (VLMs) have attempted to incorporate reasoning capabilities into visual sensing, the integration of LLMs with the millimeter-wave (mmWave) modality-despite its unique advantages under low light and occlusion-remains largely unexplored. The principal bottlenecks stem from the scarcity of radar language pairs, severe cross-dataset heterogeneity, and the absence of a foundational mmWave encoder. We address this gap through a minimal textualization interface that serializes each mmWave point cloud into concise natural language, allowing off-the-shelf LLMs to operate in a question answering (QA) setting. Building on this, we present mmWave-QA, the first benchmark for language-conditioned mmWave human perception. mmWave-QA aggregates heterogeneous public mmWave datasets and harmonizes them via calibration-aware preprocessing and global taxonomy alignment, while providing natural language QA. Spanning six scenarios and five QA tasks, the benchmark enables standardized evaluation across diverse mmWave hardware and experimental conditions, establishing a foundation for scalable research on mmWave-LLM integration. We further evaluate and analyze LLMs on our mmWave-QA, highlighting their zero-shot reasoning potential for radar perception, as well as their robustness under visual degradation.

title: HELIX: Model-Harness Co-evolution for Recursive Self-Improvement
abstract: Scaling agent capability has largely focused on improving the model, yet an interactive agent acts through a runtime harness that mediates context, tools, control flow, and stopping. The harness shapes both what a model can accomplish and the trajectories from which it learns. This coupling motivates model-harness co-evolution for recursive self-improvement: build harnesses for a fixed model, update the model from verified sibling trajectories, and rebuild the harnesses as model capabilities change. Realizing this loop requires a controlled way to evolve harnesses while preserving intervention identity and effect. We present HELIX, a source-traceable substrate for harness evolution. HELIX decomposes agent systems into typed ports, reusable atoms, recipes, product shells, and runtime policies. It makes interventions explicit and auditable while retaining trajectories, test outcomes, and provenance. Harness evolution thus serves two linked roles: improving fixed-model execution and producing matched successes, regressions, near misses, and alternative solutions as data for subsequent model improvement. We evaluate HELIX in one evolution round on code repair. A 65-candidate portfolio discovers a fixed harness that improves task coverage by 4.0% over Pi, while the full portfolio exposes up to 58.0% more verified coverage through complementary sibling behavior. Selected candidates are assessed with repeated runs and the SWE-bench evaluator. A 200-slot sibling slice yields 438 verified SFT, critic, filter, and preference records. These results show how harness, model, and data form a feedback system: harness evolution expands current capability and creates learning signal for the next model; model updates motivate the next round of harness evolution. HELIX provides an auditable interface for studying this recursive process. Code is available at https://github.com/HKUDS/HELIX.

title: Rollplex: Cross-Phase GPU Spatial Sharing for Vision Language Model Post-Training
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) enable embodied agents to reason and act from visual observations and language instructions. Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training enhances these capabilities using task feedback, but current on-policy RL runtimes execute rollout, reference scoring, and actor training in strict serial phases. While effective for text-only RL, this phase-granular execution is wasteful for VLMs, where processing dense video inputs and prompt prefixes occupies a large fraction of each phase. Because prefix processing is independent of the generated response, it can be run alongside rollout decoding, which leaves GPU compute capacity underutilized, without breaking synchronous on-policy semantics. We present Rollplex, a runtime that decomposes the reference and training phase and moves the prefix computation into the rollout decode window. Realizing this schedule requires more than concurrent kernel launches: naive colocation of Qwen2.5-VL-32\,B requires roughly 165\,GiB per GPU, while rollout and training prefer different tensor-parallel (TP) degrees and weight layouts. Rollplex addresses these constraints with two mechanisms. Phase-aware memory management controls HBM residency according to producer--consumer lifetimes. Parallelism-aware weight sharing uses the same physical storage for layout-compatible tensors across distinct TP degrees and reconstructs only incompatible tensors, avoiding a complete second actor copy. On 32 H800 GPUs, Rollplex achieves $1.23\times$--$1.30\times$ speedup over serial colocation and $1.57\times$--$2.24\times$ over disaggregation under the same GPU budget, while preserving the synchronous RL update.

title: Handover of In-Context Learning State Across Session Boundaries
abstract: This study investigates the methodological and theoretical properties of session handover in applications that use large language models. A task may continue in a new session when the context reaches the model's input limit, when the application restarts, or when another agent is asked to finish the task. The application must then decide which information from the earlier session to pass on. We formulate handover as the transfer of a task-relative in-context learning (ICL) state and distinguish exact recovery of earlier material from preservation of the target distribution. Under an exogeneity condition, predictive equivalence characterizes the coarsest deterministic sufficient handover and gives a fixed-length bit requirement. The analysis isolates the effects of the memory constraint, the writer, and the continuation procedure, and quantifies the cost of writing before the realized downstream query is known. We propose a three-part record that stores decisions and constraints exactly, uses task-justified statistics for repeated evidence, and retains original observations whose effect is not preserved by those statistics. Gaussian linear regression gives an exact finite-dimensional handover and finite-bit perturbation bounds, while nonparametric regression gives upper and lower bounds that relate memory to squared prediction error. These results provide a theory and method for deciding what a handover must retain and how its memory requirement depends on the continuation task.

title: TimeSage-EV: A Live Benchmark for Agentic Time Series Analysis in Evolving Environments
abstract: Time series analysis in high-stakes domains relies on recurring data releases, where new observations can alter the evidence base and the validity of later conclusions. Existing time series QA benchmarks mostly rely on fixed snapshots, leaving temporal validity and cutoff-aware evidence use unevaluated. We introduce TimeSage-EV, a live benchmark for agentic time series analysis in evolving environments. It tracks 60 real institutional scenarios across 6 domains, comprising 1,485 scenario-period QA pairs from Feb 2023 to May 2026 and spanning monthly, weekly, daily, and irregular release cadences. At each period, large language model (LLM) agents receive time series data and source reports, while the withheld target release provides ground truth. TimeSage-EV evaluates state identification, data summarization, and outlook reasoning. Experiments with frontier LLM agents and TimeSage-1.0, a novel self-evolving agent with a reusable analytical skill library, reveal significant performance gaps across model tiers and recurring failures in temporal validity, exogenous context use, and adaptation. We release TimeSage-EV as a research resource with monthly updates, code, a leaderboard, and failure-mode analyses.

title: IMPLEMENTASI KRIPTOGRAFI SECURE HASH ALGORITHM 256 DAN ADVANCED ENCRYPTION STANDARD 256 MODE CIPHER BLOCK CHAINING UNTUK KEAMANAN AKUN E-WALLET DENGAN TWO-FACTOR AUTHENTICATION
abstract: Keamanan akun e-wallet merupakan aspek yang sangat penting karena akun tersebut menyimpan data identitas pengguna serta memberikan akses terhadap transaksi keuangan digital yang rentan terhadap pencurian akun, penyadapan, manipulasi data, dan penyalahgunaan akses. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang, mengimplementasikan, dan memvalidasi sistem keamanan akun e-wallet menggunakan kombinasi algoritma Secure Hash Algorithm 256 (SHA-256), Advanced Encryption Standard 256 (AES-256) dengan mode Cipher Block Chaining (CBC), serta mekanisme Two-Factor Authentication (2FA). Algoritma SHA-256 digunakan untuk menghasilkan nilai hash dari identitas pengguna sebagai bentuk perlindungan terhadap data autentikasi, sedangkan AES-256 mode CBC digunakan untuk mengenkripsi nilai hash tersebut sehingga kerahasiaan data tetap terjaga selama proses penyimpanan. Mekanisme 2FA diterapkan melalui verifikasi One-Time Password (OTP) sebagai lapisan keamanan tambahan setelah proses autentikasi tahap pertama berhasil dilakukan. Sistem diimplementasikan ke dalam sebuah aplikasi berbasis Graphical User Interface (GUI) menggunakan bahasa pemrograman Python. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa aplikasi yang dibangun mampu melakukan proses registrasi, login, dan verifikasi OTP sesuai dengan rancangan sistem. Proses validasi dilakukan melalui beberapa skenario pengujian, yaitu autentikasi menggunakan kredensial yang benar, penggunaan kata sandi yang salah, modifikasi data terenkripsi, serta penghapusan data terenkripsi. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa sistem mampu mendeteksi setiap kondisi tersebut secara tepat sehingga keamanan, integritas, dan kerahasiaan data akun e-wallet dapat terjaga dengan baik. The security of e-wallet accounts has become increasingly important because these accounts store user’s personal information and provide access to digital financial transactions that are vulnerable to account theft, interception, data manipulation, and unauthorized access. This research aims to design, implement, and validate an e-wallet account security system by integrating the Secure Hash Algorithm 256 (SHA-256), Advanced Encryption Standard 256 (AES-256) in Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode, and Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) mechanism. The SHA-256 algorithm is employed to generate a hash value of the user’s identity as a means of protecting authentication data, while AES-256 in CBC mode is used to encrypt the hash value to ensure data confidentiality during storage. The Two-Factor Authentication mechanism is implemented through One Time Password (OTP) verification as an additional layer of security after the first authentication stage has been successfully completed. The system is implemented as a Graphical User Interface (GUI)-based application using the Python programming language. The results demonstrate that the developed application successfully performs user registration, login, and OTP verification in accordance with the proposed system design. The validation process is conducted through several authentication scenarios, including the use of valid credentials, incorrect passwords, modified encrypted data, and deleted encrypted data. The testing results indicate that the system accurately detects each of these conditions, thereby ensuring the security, integrity, and confidentiality of e-wallet account data.

Algoritma SHA-256 digunakan untuk menghasilkan nilai hash dari identitas pengguna sebagai bentuk perlindungan terhadap data autentikasi, sedangkan AES-256 mode CBC digunakan untuk mengenkripsi nilai hash tersebut sehingga kerahasiaan data tetap terjaga selama proses penyimpanan. Mekanisme 2FA diterapkan melalui verifikasi One-Time Password (OTP) sebagai lapisan keamanan tambahan setelah proses autentikasi tahap pertama berhasil dilakukan. Sistem diimplementasikan ke dalam sebuah aplikasi berbasis Graphical User Interface (GUI) menggunakan bahasa pemrograman Python. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa aplikasi yang dibangun mampu melakukan proses registrasi, login, dan verifikasi OTP sesuai dengan rancangan sistem. Proses validasi dilakukan melalui beberapa skenario pengujian, yaitu autentikasi menggunakan kredensial yang benar, penggunaan kata sandi yang salah, modifikasi data terenkripsi, serta penghapusan data terenkripsi. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa sistem mampu mendeteksi setiap kondisi tersebut secara tepat sehingga keamanan, integritas, dan kerahasiaan data akun e-wallet dapat terjaga dengan baik. The security of e-wallet accounts has become increasingly important because these accounts store user’s personal information and provide access to digital financial transactions that are vulnerable to account theft, interception, data manipulation, and unauthorized access. This research aims to design, implement, and validate an e-wallet account security system by integrating the Secure Hash Algorithm 256 (SHA-256), Advanced Encryption Standard 256 (AES-256) in Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode, and Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) mechanism. The SHA-256 algorithm is employed to generate a hash value of the user’s identity as a means of protecting authentication data, while AES-256 in CBC mode is used to encrypt the hash value to ensure data confidentiality during storage. The Two-Factor Authentication mechanism is implemented through One Time Password (OTP) verification as an additional layer of security after the first authentication stage has been successfully completed. The system is implemented as a Graphical User Interface (GUI)-based application using the Python programming language. The results demonstrate that the developed application successfully performs user registration, login, and OTP verification in accordance with the proposed system design. The validation process is conducted through several authentication scenarios, including the use of valid credentials, incorrect passwords, modified encrypted data, and deleted encrypted data. The testing results indicate that the system accurately detects each of these conditions, thereby ensuring the security, integrity, and confidentiality of e-wallet account data.

title: An Effective Centralized Admission System Adopted for All Government Universities in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Over the last decade, statistics show an exponential rise of enrolment to the Saudi Arabian public universities from around 82,075 in the 1990s to 339,836 in the previous years. This has been made possible by the Saudi government which has been investing a lot of resources in the education sector. The private corporations have also participated in empowering this sector. Secondary graduates are encouraged to further their education to the University level to sharpen their skills for better job opportunities (Murphey, chap. 8, doc.13). There are about 24 public universities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA). For students to be admitted in these universities, they are required to submit an application for each university. On the other hand, universities set up admission boards that go through each application before choosing which applicants to admit. This process is quite tedious and time consuming both for the applicants and the universities. The objective of this paper is to design and implement a Centralised Admission System (CAS) using the current technology to facilitate and ease the admission process. With CAS, applicants will not have to repeat the application process for each university. Rather, they will only submit one application. The system will rank the students and allocate them to the universities depending on their scores. Universities will not have to go through the tedious process of choosing qualified students, since the system will use a verified algorithm in determining the qualified applicants. With this system, there will be transparency in the admission process and students will not have to spend a lot of time in the process. The system will make work easier for all the stakeholders. My recommendation is that the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Ministry of Higher Learning will embrace this new technology and encourage efficiency and effectiveness in the university admission process.

title: From Backstory to State: Causal Tests of Synthetic Autobiographical Conditioning in Artificial Decision Systems
abstract: Prospective Research Note proposing a falsifiable composite-agent architecture and controlled experiment to distinguish decorative synthetic backstory, raw-record retrieval, prompt steering, and implementation failure from a causally effective compact persistent decision state after source removal. The primary total-effect estimand uses aligned slotwise categorical divergence; the stronger feedback-modulated endpoint uses a three-category outcome and a preregistered pre-feedback separation gate. No empirical result or claim of consciousness, sentience, personhood, subjective autonomy, or metaphysical free will is made. No external funding was received; the work was self-funded by the author.

title: QTT Carrier-Deletion Finite-Window and Timing-Access Blind Test Extension
abstract: Erase the apparent carrier. Recover the qubit from its halo. Then ask a different clock. This preregistration separates an ordinary quantum-memory qualification from a distinct timing test. Test A evolves a logical qubit through a frozen local channel, physically resets its original carrier, and asks whether a finite surrounding window can recover it. Test B asks whether that independently reconstructed channel fidelity controls a separate timing-covariance frontier. Test A: where is the recoverable channel? \[ \mathcal R_i(\omega)=|0\rangle\!\langle0|_i\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_i\omega, \] \[ Q_{\rm del}=2F_{\rm avg}(\mathcal N_{\rm del},\operatorname{id})-1, \qquad \boxed{F_e^{\rm del}=\frac{1+3Q_{\rm del}}4.} \] Target-only and every smaller halo subwindow remain optimized counterfactuals. A physical reset, sham reset, hidden-record injection, boundary ladder, and complete terminal record are required before the recovery layer qualifies. Test B: does the memory verifier intertwine with an independent timing projector? \[ \boxed{W^\dagger M_eW=P_{\rm align}}, \qquad \eta_T=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_{\rm align}), \] \[ \mathcal U_T^\star =\inf 2\sqrt{\det\Sigma_{T\Omega}}. \] On the certified canonical branch, the sealed QTT target is \[ \boxed{ \eta_T=F_e^{\rm del}, \qquad \mathcal U_T^\star=1-F_e^{\rm del}. } \] No complement coefficient is fitted. Five fidelity corridors, a radius/depth ladder, one-third untouched holdouts, topology twins, full covariance, global five-sigma decisions, at least 95% planned power, and transfer to a second record technology are frozen before data. The external computation is a feasibility anchor, not the timing target An, Cao, and Cui report carrier-deletion recovery in a local kicked-Ising memory. Their result qualifies the plausibility of Test A. Their reported \(Q=0.516\) is explicitly forbidden from constructing Test B. The public source archive lacks the exact arrays and scripts, so exact replication remains pending. Five terminal outcomes INELIGIBLE_NO_THEORY_VERDICT REGISTERED_QTT_CONSEQUENCE_FALSIFIED QTT_CANDIDATE QUALIFIED_OTHER_OR_CROSS_CHANNEL_ANOMALY AMBIGUOUS_OR_UNDERPOWERED Any failed eligibility gate terminates without a theory verdict. A positive result requires the full multirung shape, not one selected point. An off-target anomaly is preserved rather than discarded or used as a post-hoc rescue. Immutable protocol seal eb0640b25c1d0bde56cacc7f25d9ce4304594833e4aa937ed50293a1faafc849 This is a separate sealed extension. It changes no target, threshold, classifier, protocol hash, or file in the parent test under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21902885. Public anchors Completed-record fan-out and timing-access framework Observation as Access Quantum Traction Theory: Main Book External finite-window recovery paper The PDF is the default preview. The reconstruction archive contains the sealed JSON, classifier, eighteen-gate and raw-terminal templates, Stage-0 handoff, verifier, external audit, adversarial review, metadata, and checksums.

title: dark-matter-quantum-sim v2.1: DM-003 erratum — bitstring extraction defect corrected (FAIL→PASS)
abstract: Erratum for DM-003-ibmq-v1. The original DM-003 IBM Quantum runner extracted the spin-flip probability from the wrong Qiskit bitstring ('10' = initial state instead of '01' = target state). The published FAIL verdict (99.6% error) is incorrect; the hardware actually produced a PASS (2.0% error, 98.0% flip probability vs analytic 100%). This deposit contains: (1) the erratum document, (2) the corrected runner, and (3) the corrected ProofRecord. The original ProofRecord is preserved unchanged in the repository. GitHub: ERRATUM_DM-003.md

title: Natural language processing-based detection and classification of periphrastic expressions in Uzbek text corpora
abstract: In this study, a Natural Language Processing-based framework for the detection and linguopragmatic classification of periphrastic expressions in Uzbek text corpora is proposed. The current state of research on figurative and pragmatically enriched language processing is analyzed in relation to the limited computational treatment of Uzbek periphrastic expressions. The linguistic and functional properties of periphrastic expressions are examined as indirect, descriptive, and context-dependent discourse units. A hybrid methodology is developed by combining corpus preparation, morphology-sensitive preprocessing, rule-guided candidate extraction, weighted detection, and functional classification. The detected expressions are classified into evaluative, euphemistic, expressive, referential, and stylistic categories according to their dominant linguopragmatic function. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework identifies Uzbek periphrastic expressions with stable overall performance and shows higher effectiveness for categories supported by clearer lexical and contextual markers. The role of discourse analysis in improving computational interpretation of non-literal language is established. The proposed approach is presented as a practical basis for corpus annotation, semantic search, stylistic profiling, discourse-sensitive text mining, and the further development of intelligent Uzbek language technologies.

title: Temporal graph transformer for next visit diagnosis prediction on electronic health records
abstract: Next-visit diagnosis prediction with electronic health records (EHR) is critical for proactive medicine, but mainstream methods fail to simultaneously capture cross-visit temporal dependencies, inter-medical-event structural associations and the patient-visit-code hierarchical semantic relationships in EHR, and lack clinical interpretability. This study proposes EHRFormer, a temporal graph transformer model for EHR-based next-visit diagnosis prediction. We first construct a patient-specific temporal heterogeneous graph with timestamped visit nodes and heterogeneous medical event nodes to decouple medical event semantics and visit temporal states, and model intra-visit structural and cross-visit temporal relationships via two types of heterogeneous edges. A temporal-aware heterogeneous message passing mechanism integrated with Time2Vec-based time encoding is designed to fuse temporal and structural information, and meta-path-based global positional and local structural encoding are introduced to capture high-order medical event interactions. Additionally, a patient graph explainer module is developed to identify prediction-critical subgraphs and medical events for clinical interpretability. Extensive experiments on three real-world EHR datasets (MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, MarketScan CCAE) with core metrics of visit-level precision@k and code-level accuracy@k demonstrate that EHRFormer achieves state-of-the-art performance, strong noise robustness, and high inference efficiency with linear time complexity. The graph explainer can accurately identify clinically meaningful medical events consistent with clinical guidelines. EHRFormer realizes collaborative learning of EHR’s three-level hierarchical representations, unifying high prediction accuracy, reliable clinical interpretability and efficient inference, and provides a novel paradigm for EHR-based medical predictive modeling with notable clinical application value.

title: Style or Signature? Artist-Disjoint Evaluation of Style Classification in Frozen Vision Embeddings
abstract: Frozen image embeddings from models such as CLIP are increasingly used to classify paintings by art-historical style, with high reported accuracy. We ask whether this accuracy reflects an understanding of style or the recognition of individual artists. Standard evaluation uses random splits in which works by the same artist appear on both sides, so a classifier can succeed by recognising the painter rather than the movement. We re-evaluate style classification under an artist-disjoint protocol, holding out every artist in turn so that no work is ever classified using other works by its own painter. On a balanced dataset of 320 paintings across four twentieth-century movements, 5-NN style accuracy falls from 0.87 to 0.77 under this protocol, and the drop is sharply uneven. Impressionism and Cubism barely move, while Surrealism falls twenty points. The pattern holds across four image encoders, including a vision-only self-supervised model, which places the effect in visual structure rather than language. Where an encoder captures genuine shared form, individual artists are barely recognisable yet style is robust, while Surrealism shows the opposite. We argue that artist-disjoint evaluation is necessary to measure stylistic understanding in frozen embeddings.

title: AT-ADD: All-Type Audio Deepfake Detection Challenge Summary
abstract: This paper summarizes the ACM Multimedia 2026 AT-ADD Grand Challenge on all-type audio deepfake detection. AT-ADD contains two tracks: robust speech deepfake detection under realistic acoustic and channel variations, and type-agnostic detection over speech, environmental sound, singing voice, and music. We describe the challenge tasks, dataset and evaluation-set design, official leaderboard results, and common design patterns observed in participating systems. The best Track 1 system achieved 90.71% Macro-F1 on the final evaluation set, while the best Track 2 system achieved 96.10% Macro-F1. The final submissions show that strong systems commonly combine large-scale self-supervised audio representations, data augmentation, multi-crop inference, and structured fusion or routing. The results also reveal remaining challenges in generalization to unseen generators, robustness to realistic speech-domain distortions, and balanced performance across heterogeneous audio types.

title: Local geometry for Schmidt number witnesses
abstract: Suppose that $F_E$ is the face of the convex set of all $m\otimes n$ bi-partite states which consists of states with ranges contained in a subspace $E$. For generic subspaces $E$ with a specific dimension, we use the result in [Phys. Rev. A 112 (2025), 032426] to see that there exists a number $κ$, depending only on the dimension of $E$, such that there exist Schmidt number $\ell$ witnesses outside of $F_{E^\perp}$ if and only if $\ell\leκ$. In this generic case, we show in this paper that there exist Schmidt number $\ell$ witnesses for $\ell>κ$ around the projection states located at the center of $F_{E^\perp}$.

title: LightTeaNet: A Weakly Supervised Lightweight CNN for Multi-Label Tea Leaf Disease Detection and Localization
abstract: Tea is known as an important crop in many parts of South and Southeast Asia, yet the production of tea is still hampered by the multiple diseases that decrease the quantity and quality. Traditional methods of inspection, which are manual, are not consistent, labor-intensive, and depend on extensive monitoring. This paper introduces a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) designed for weakly supervised multi-label classification and disease localization in tea leaves called LightTeaNet. LightTeaNet learns directly from image-level labels and employs Class Activation Mapping (CAM) to localize disease-affected regions automatically, unlike conventional object detection models such as YOLO, which require extensive bounding box annotations. For Parameter efficiency, the network integrates Depthwise Separable Convolutions, and for enhanced feature discrimination, it integrates Channel Attention. LightTeaNet has achieved a Precision of 0.9615, a Recall of 0.8772, and an F1-score of 0.9179, while it shows mAP@0.50=0.1810 without any manual annotations, which delivers a competitive localization performance in the experimental results. These results validate the model as an interpretable as well as a resource-efficient framework for intelligent disease monitoring in agriculture.

title: Fast Implicit Neural Light Field Representation via Geometric Decomposition and Multi-Resolution Low-Rank Features
abstract: Implicit neural representations provide a compact and continuous way to reconstruct dense light fields from sampled ray coordinates. However, fast light field reconstruction remains challenging because a light field is a high-dimensional signal with strong spatial-angular redundancy and structured disparity variations. Directly fitting 4D ray coordinates with a neural network often requires considerable optimization time to recover both view appearance and cross-view consistency. To address this issue, this paper proposes a fast implicit light field representation based on geometric decomposition and multi-resolution low-rank features. The proposed method decomposes a 4D light field into a horizontal disparity plane, a spatial texture plane, and a vertical disparity plane. Each plane is represented by a low-rank structure that combines a low-resolution 2D grid with the element-wise product of two high-resolution 1D line features at multiple resolution levels. The fused features are decoded by a lightweight multilayer perceptron to predict RGB values. Experiments on public light field datasets show that the proposed method achieves competitive reconstruction quality while providing a better trade-off among model parameters, training time, and inference efficiency.

title: Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Model Merging
abstract: Model merging combines trained models directly in weight space, offering a compute-efficient alternative to additional fine-tuning. Selecting merge parameters is nevertheless difficult because downstream evaluations are expensive, gradients are unavailable, and source capabilities can conflict. We formulate merge-parameter selection as a black-box multi-objective optimization problem and introduce MOBO-Merge, a merge-operator agnostic framework that uses multi-objective Bayesian optimization to approximate the Pareto front under a limited evaluation budget. We evaluate Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.1-8B in two-model instruction-math and three-model instruction-math-code settings using Linear, SLERP, TIES, and block-wise merge operators. On held-out benchmark partitions, MOBO-Merge obtains higher mean hypervolume than random search in 11 of 12 reported comparisons. The gain is small for one-dimensional Linear interpolation but substantially larger for several TIES, block-wise, and three-objective searches. No merge operator is uniformly best: TIES leads in three of four family-setting combinations, whereas Block-Linear 4x is strongest for the Llama three-model merge. These results show that multi-objective Bayesian optimization is valuable as a search layer for expressive merge parameterizations.

title: IMPLEMENTASI DYNAMIC DIFFICULTY ADJUSTMENT BERBASIS ALPHADDA UNTUK GAME BALANCING PADA BOARD GAME CONGKLAK
abstract: Penurunan minat terhadap permainan rakyat seperti Congklak mendorong perlunya adaptasi digital yang mampu menjaga keseimbangan permainan (game balance). Penelitian ini bertujuan mengimplementasikan AlphaDDA—mekanisme Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment (DDA) berbasis AlphaZero—pada board game Congklak serta mengevaluasi efektivitasnya berdasarkan gameplay metrics selisih skor (Δscore) dan durasi bermain (playtime). Metodologi penelitian menggunakan Design Science Research Methodology (DSRM). Model dasar AlphaZero dilatih melalui self-play hingga mencapai peringkat kemahiran 1729,31 Elo selama 50 turnamen round-robin, membuktikan keunggulan atas agen Random dan MCTS serta performa yang kompetitif terhadap agen Minimax. Difficulty adjustment mechanism dieksekusi secara dinamis dengan mengubah jumlah simulasi Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) berdasarkan estimasi value. Efektivitas AlphaDDA dievaluasi melalui eksperimen within-subject pada 10 partisipan untuk membandingkan kondisi DDA dan non-DDA menggunakan paired samples t-test. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kondisi DDA secara signifikan berhasil mempersempit rata-rata Δscore menjadi 11,80 poin berbanding 26,00 poin pada kondisi non-DDA (p=0,011<0,05) dengan ukuran efek besar (d=-0,87). Sementara itu, playtime tidak menunjukkan perbedaan yang signifikan secara statistik (p=0,798>0,05), yang menunjukkan bahwa AlphaDDA tidak memengaruhi engagement. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa algoritma AlphaDDA terbukti efektif untuk game balancing pada board game Congklak, tetapi tidak efektif untuk meningkatkan engagement pada board game Congklak. ---------- The declining popularity of traditional folk games such as Congklak underscores the need for digital adaptations capable of maintaining game balance. This study aims to implement AlphaDDA—an AlphaZero-based Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment (DDA) mechanism—in the Congklak board game and evaluate its effectiveness using gameplay metrics of score difference (Δscore) and playing duration (playtime). The research methodology employs the Design Science Research Methodology (DSRM). A baseline AlphaZero model was trained via self-play, achieving a proficiency rating of 1729.31 Elo across 50 round-robin tournaments, demonstrating superiority over Random and MCTS agents as well as competitive performance against the Minimax agent. The difficulty adjustment mechanism was executed dynamically by modifying Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) simulation budgets based on value estimates. The effectiveness of AlphaDDA was evaluated through a within-subject experiment involving 10 participants, comparing DDA and non-DDA conditions via paired samples t-tests. The results demonstrate that the DDA condition significantly narrowed the average Δscore to 11.80 points compared to 26.00 points in the non-DDA condition (p=0.011<0.05) with a large effect size (d=-0.87). Meanwhile, playtime showed no statistically significant difference (p=0.798>0,05), indicating that AlphaDDA did not affect engagement. This study concludes that the AlphaDDA algorithm is effective for game balancing in the Congklak board game, but not effective for increasing engagement in the Congklak board game.

title: Empirical Validation and Engineering-Hardened Execution of the CNVS Framework
abstract: Note: In this new version 3.0 the concept of Invariant Control Graph G_i(t) is introduced, decoupled from the other two Graphs, for the processing of the Global Verification Function.This report presents the empirical engineering validation of the Closed Native Verification Systems (CNVS) framework. It evaluates the architecture's capability to execute distributed state validation without relying on traditional terminal-consensus mechanisms, utilizing instead geometric invariants and topological decoupling. Through high-resolution Monte Carlo simulations (up to 500,000 iterations per configuration), the study analyzes the framework across three primary executable domains: Test 13 evaluates fragmentation sensitivity within a 256-bit CSPRNG-hardened finite field, demonstrating strict alignment between empirical reconstruction rates and exact injective hypergeometric references. Test 14 executes a full semantic pipeline on a simulated physical domain, proving that the progressive global invariant effectively intercepts and rejects locally admissible "stealth" attacks up to extreme collusion thresholds. Furthermore, it models progressive invariant leakage, demonstrating resistance to false-state bypass under partial disclosure. Test 15 isolates the critical fragmentation cardinality parameter (m), confirming that scaling m from 32 to 512 exponentially shifts adversarial reconstruction success toward higher compromise thresholds, without inducing macroscopic degradation in local computational latency or validation throughput. The consolidated empirical data validates the structural and mathematical consistency of the CNVS theoretical model in an identifying regime, providing an executable foundation for subsequent real-world distributed network deployments.

title: An anomaly detection model for shared service data ingestion integrating rule constraints and attention mechanisms
abstract: To solve the problems of inconsistent format of multi-source fields, difficult identification of rule boundary samples, and high missed detection rate of cross-field conflicts in the storage verification of shared data services, an abnormal record detection model was constructed. In the model, the input tensor was generated by field cleaning, rule mapping and record level feature encoding, taking interface input log, message queue drop record and master data synchronization check record as sample sources. In the detection stage, the field correlation modeling, attention weight allocation and rule constraint loss are fused to output the anomaly score and complete the threshold decision. The experiment constructed a data set based on 1,086,420 valid records within 30 consecutive days, and 103,684 abnormal samples. The test results show that the Precision, Recall, F1 and AUC of the model reach 0.946, 0.928, 0.937 and 0.962, respectively, and the false alarm rate is reduced to 0.024. The inference time of a single record is 6.5 ms, which is 0.124 higher than that of the rule detection method.

title: Design and implementation of a big data-driven intelligent early warning system for psychological crises among vocational college students
abstract: A big data-driven intelligent early warning system for psychological crises among vocational college students is presented in this study, addressing the urgent need for precise, real-time mental health risk identification in complex educational environments. Leveraging a cloud-native Lambda architecture, the system integrates high-frequency heterogeneous behavioral data from campus sources and applies advanced feature engineering to construct a unified, robust data foundation. By combining gradient boosting machines and deep neural network models to improve recognition accuracy and support dynamic adaptation to diverse individual patterns. The core components of the system include alert propagation based on RESTful API for automatic adjustment of multi-level alert sensitivity thresholds; additionally, distributed feature storage to ensure model consistency between offline training and real-time inference; and distributed use of feature storage. Kubernetes orchestration deployment allows the system to quickly allocate resources and handle event streams under high concurrency, while also enabling system scalability. Pilot data from empirical evaluation agencies indicate that the intervention has significantly improved the lead time for actionable interventions, the false positive rate, and the accuracy of early warnings. Results confirm the practical effectiveness of explainable artificial intelligence in augmenting campus crisis management workflows and provide a rigorous baseline for the future development of integrated mental health support platforms.

title: ER-KANs: Efficient and Robust Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Data-Scarce Scientific Machine Learning
abstract: The efficient-KAN literature---covering Chebyshev, wavelet, and radial-basis-function variants of the original Kolmogorov-Arnold Network---has been benchmarked almost entirely on clean data. We show that this choice conceals a large capability difference between architectures: ChebyKAN's test MSE (evaluated against clean ground truth) increases by a factor of 10.6x when training data is corrupted with sigma=0.1 noise, versus 7.9x for vanilla KAN, 1.7x for a standard MLP, and just 1.4x for our proposed ER-KAN. ER-KAN combines three design choices targeting the noisy, data-scarce setting: shared Gaussian RBF bases across all edges in a layer (providing locality and efficient parameterisation), curriculum noise injection during training (explicitly teaching noise robustness), and entropy-weighted adaptive regularisation (preventing overfitting at small N). The result is a 595-parameter network that matches MLP accuracy at moderate noise while degrading far more gracefully as noise grows. We evaluate on eight analytic functions (N in {50, 200, 500}, sigma in {0, 0.03, 0.1}), on a damped harmonic oscillator physics-informed neural network where ER-KAN achieves 4.2x lower solution MSE than MLP, and on a Burgers' equation PINN where all models fail to converge---a genuine limitation we report rather than suppress. We introduce the noise degradation ratio as a simple complementary metric and recommend it become a standard reporting requirement for efficient-KAN papers.

title: Structure-Guided Spatiotemporal Attention Graph Neural Network for Traffic Flow Prediction
abstract: Deep spatiotemporal models integrating graph convolutions and attention mechanisms have demonstrated excellent performance in network-level traffic flow prediction, owing to their exceptional ability to capture complex spatiotemporal dependencies. Despite their predictive success, deployment of such models in safety-critical urban systems remains constrained by their inherent lack of transparency. Existing post-hoc diagnostic methods often struggle with spurious correlations and fail to unveil the intrinsic decision-making mechanisms governing traffic dynamics, resulting in suboptimal interpretability and limited operational trustworthiness. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the Structure-Guided Spatiotemporal Attention Graph Neural Network (SGSAN). Departing from traditional architectures that rely on unconstrained adaptive graphs, SGSAN explicitly learns a static Directed Dependency Graph (DDG) to identify the invariant macroscopic propagation paths of traffic states. We further introduce an InfoNCE-based soft-coupling mechanism that anchors the model's dynamic spatiotemporal attention to this structural prior, offering a mechanistic account of the model's decision-making process while ensuring robust forecasting by aligning attention-based reasoning with identified macroscopic dependencies and preventing over-reliance on ephemeral local noise. Furthermore, a decoupled two-stage optimization framework is developed to resolve the fundamental conflict between structural discovery and predictive error minimization. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that SGSAN achieves state-of-the-art predictive accuracy while providing built-in interpretability that organically aligns with the physical logic of traffic networks.

title: When Does More Correct Data Hurt? Insertion-Stability and the Limits of Dimension-Based Theory
abstract: Adding data known to be correct ought to be safe. Not always. Larsen, Pabbaraju and Shetty model the failure with a monotone adversary, which reads an i.i.d. training sample and may append as many further examples as it likes, provided the target hypothesis labels them all. Mehrotra has since settled the cost, showing that for classes of VC dimension d >= 2 no learner can guarantee expected error better than Theta((d/n)log(en/d)), a logarithmic factor above the clean PAC rate. Because that rate is a worst case over all classes, it says nothing about which classes actually suffer the penalty, and the answer turns on the learner. We call a learner insertion-stable if feeding it more correctly labeled examples can only shrink the region where it errs. Such learners are immune to the adversary, since on any given sample the risk after insertions never exceeds the risk on the clean part alone, however much is added and however cleverly it is chosen. High- probability guarantees carry over unchanged, and because Closure is insertion-stable every intersection-closed class keeps its clean rate of E[Err] <= (21d+34)/n. Immunity is not something the classical dimensions can predict. Two classes can agree on VCdim = Ldim = 2 and still split, one at Theta(1/n) and the other at Theta(log(en)/n), while intervals have unbounded Littlestone dimension and are immune anyway. On Mehrotra's hard class we prove more than the failure of a single algorithm, showing that no monotone permutation-invariant compression scheme of any finite size attains the clean rate. The question is therefore not whether a class is hard, nor whether a learner is good, but whether the two suit each other. Given an insertion-stable learner that is optimal on clean data, correct additions are free, and without one the cost belongs to the class, so changing the learner will not avoid it.

The question is therefore not whether a class is hard, nor whether a learner is good, but whether the two suit each other. Given an insertion-stable learner that is optimal on clean data, correct additions are free, and without one the cost belongs to the class, so changing the learner will not avoid it.

title: Do Tabular Foundation Models Still Need Feature Engineering?
abstract: Feature engineering has long been a cornerstone of tabular machine learning. Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are pretrained on a wide range of tabular datasets and applied via in-context learning. Their rise raises a natural question: does manual feature construction still matter as these models become more capable? To answer this, we perform a controlled study across several versions of two major TFM families, testing a wide range of existing feature engineering techniques on benchmark datasets from TabArena. We find a consistent pattern: feature engineering gains are concentrated in earlier model generations and become negligible for the strongest models. These results suggest that stronger TFMs depend less on explicitly engineered input representations. In a complementary experiment, however, adding in-context information from related datasets still improves performance. Our findings indicate a shift in the source of performance gains for stronger TFMs: re-representing existing inputs becomes less effective, while providing additional task-relevant context remains beneficial.

title: ANALISIS KINERJA KOHERENSI NARATIF DAN FAITHFULNESS PADA SISTEM AGENTIC Al DAN LIGHTRAG UNTUK PEMBELAJARAN BERBASIS CERITA
abstract: Pembelajaran berbasis cerita membantu penyampaian materi abstrak, tetapi generasi teks panjang menggunakan large language models (LLM) masih menghasilkan kesalahan faktual pada lebih dari 50 persen konten serta rentan terhadap inkoherensi naratif. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) memitigasi halusinasi, tetapi representasi data datar membatasi pemahaman antarkonsep. Untuk mengatasinya, LightRAG berbasis knowledge graph dan agentic AI yang memiliki kemampuan perencanaan, pemanfaatan alat, serta refleksi diri diintegrasikan. Penelitian ini mengevaluasi kinerja integrasi agentic AI dan LightRAG dalam menghasilkan cerita pembelajaran berdasarkan koherensi naratif dan faithfulness. Penelitian menggunakan design research methodology (DRM) empat tahap untuk merumuskan masalah hingga mengevaluasi sistem. Knowledge graph dibangun dari dataset WikiEval. Pengujian menggunakan 200 cerita yang terdiri atas 100 cerita dari baseline (Gemini 2.5 Flash) dan 100 keluaran agentic AI dalam bahasa Indonesia dan Inggris. Koherensi naratif dievaluasi menggunakan G-Eval, sedangkan faithfulness diukur dengan RAGAS dan FABLES melalui pendekatan LLM-as-a-judge yang divalidasi ahli. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan peningkatan skor koherensi naratif sebesar 11,0%, dari 4,122 pada sistem baseline ke 4,574 pada sistem agentic AI. Skor RAGAS meningkat sebesar 12,0%, dari 0,827 ke 0,926, sedangkan skor FABLES tidak menunjukkan perbedaan signifikan dengan skor 0,991 pada baseline dan 0,990 pada agentic AI. Rata-rata jumlah klaim per cerita berkurang 41,6%, dan proporsi klaim tanpa bukti tekstual turun dari 9,24% ke 2,96%. Hasil ini membuktikan bahwa pembagian peran kognitif dalam sistem agentic AI dan LightRAG efektif mengatasi keterbatasan LLM terhadap inkoherensi naratif dan halusinasi. ------------ Story-based learning aids in delivering abstract concepts, but long-text generation using large language models (LLMs) still produces factual errors in over 50 percent of content and remains prone to narrative incoherence. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mitigates hallucinations, but flat data representation limits cross-conceptual understanding. To address this, a knowledge graph-based LightRAG and agentic AI, featuring planning, tool use, and self-reflection capabilities, are integrated. This study evaluates the performance of integrating agentic AI and LightRAG in generating educational stories based on narrative coherence and faithfulness. The study employs a four-stage design research methodology (DRM) from problem formulation to system evaluation. The knowledge graph is constructed from the WikiEval dataset. Testing utilizes 200 stories, comprising 100 stories from the baseline (Gemini 2.5 Flash) and 100 outputs from agentic AI in Indonesian and English. Narrative coherence is evaluated using G-Eval, while faithfulness is measured using RAGAS and FABLES via an expert-validated LLM-as-a-judge approach. The results show an 11.0% increase in narrative coherence score, from 4.122 in the baseline system to 4.574 in the agentic AI system. The RAGAS score increased by 12.0%, from 0.827 to 0.926, whereas the FABLES score showed no significant difference with scores of 0.991 in the baseline and 0.990 in agentic AI. The average number of claims per story decreased by 41.6%, and the proportion of claims without textual evidence dropped from 9.24% to 2.96%. These findings prove that cognitive role allocation within agentic AI and LightRAG systems effectively overcomes LLM limitations regarding narrative incoherence and hallucination.

title: Artificial Intelligence Laboratory Manual: Examples and Practical Exercises
abstract: Artificial Intelligence Laboratory Manual: Practical Examples and Exercises is a practical educational resource designed to support hands-on learning of fundamental concepts and techniques in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). The manual presents a structured collection of practical examples, guided exercises, and implementation-based activities that help learners understand AI concepts through hands-on experimentation. It focuses on developing practical skills by combining essential theoretical concepts with step-by-step computational exercises and programming-based implementations. The material is intended for students, educators, and independent learners who wish to develop foundational practical skills in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. Its general structure makes it suitable for use across different academic disciplines and educational settings. The manual may be used as a laboratory companion, classroom teaching resource, self-learning guide, or supplementary material for courses involving Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, data analysis, and related computational techniques. Key features include: Practical examples for understanding fundamental AI and ML concepts. Step-by-step exercises designed to develop hands-on implementation skills. Programming-based activities and computational experimentation. Exercises that reinforce theoretical concepts through practical implementation. A structured format suitable for classroom laboratory sessions and independent learning. This publication is intended to provide an accessible and practical foundation for learners beginning their journey in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.

title: SETT Framework: 技術的主張とアーキテクチャ方針
abstract: SETT(Scalable Expert-based Task Topology)は、確率的推論と運用権限を明示的に分離することを基本設計とするマルチエージェントAIフレームワークである。本技術レポートは、SETT v0.12.0 時点におけるアーキテクチャ上の主張と技術的立場をまとめたものであり、明示的な責務の所有、Actions as Data、決定論的ガバナンス、因果トレーシング、実行ライフサイクル制御、協調的キャンセル、deadline、構造化された終端状態、および実世界への作用境界における冪等性を対象とする。 本レポートでは、SETT のアーキテクチャ進化における主要な節目、現時点での検証結果、既知の限界、ならびに中心的な主張が弱められる、または反証され得る条件を整理する。本版の作成にあたり、SETT v0.12.0 のソースアーカイブを独立したレビュー環境で実行し、全テストスイートは 893/893 件すべて合格した。この結果は、テスト対象となった契約との整合性を示すものであり、セキュリティ認証、普遍的な正しさの証明、あるいは第三者による独立検証を意味するものではない。 SETT は現在も継続的に開発されている。API、内部構造、実装機構、過去の設計判断は、テスト、ベンチマーク、外部レビュー、および実際の利用から得られる新たな証拠に基づき、拡張、見直し、置換、あるいは必要に応じて撤回される可能性がある。したがって、本レポートは SETT v0.12.0 の技術的スナップショットであり、最終的なアーキテクチャを宣言するものではない。 本プロジェクトが継続して維持することを意図する原則は、能力が自動的に権限を意味してはならないこと、推論・認可・作用を区別可能な状態に保つこと、ガバナンスを明示的かつ監査可能にすること、そして技術的主張を常に検証および反証の対象として開いておくことである。実装上の重要な変更、完了した作業、既知の限界、今後の発展については、SETT の公開リポジトリおよび 4HumanityAI を通じて継続的に追跡可能な状態を維持する。 本レコードは公式日本語版である。英語版を本技術レポートの基準版(canonical edition)とし、スペイン語版も公式な言語別版として独立したレコードで公開している。 関連出版物:本技術レポートは、SETT の先行日本語プレプリント(DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21301700)で提示したアーキテクチャ上の方向性を発展・更新したものである。本レポートでは、SETT v0.12.0 時点におけるフレームワークの技術的立場、アーキテクチャの進化、ガバナンス境界、実装から得られた検証結果、および既知の限界に重点を置く。 公式他言語版:英語基準版: SETT Framework: Technical Thesis and Architectural Position — DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21926841スペイン語版: SETT Framework: Tesis técnica y posición arquitectónica — DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21927405

title: Research on the Impact of AI Customer Service Recommendations on Consumers' Online Purchase Intention Across Different Service Scenarios
abstract: This dataset contains anonymized survey data collected for a study examining the impact of AI versus human customer service recommendations on consumers' online purchase intention across different service scenarios (cognitive-analytical vs. emotional-social), with technology readiness as a moderating variable. The study employed a between-groups experimental design. Data were collected from adult consumers with online shopping experience through Credamo, a professional online research data platform in China, using fully anonymous data collection mode. No personally identifiable information was collected at any stage.

title: STRAP: a deep learning-based predictive framework with low-latency evaluation for real-time streaming data
abstract: With the advancement of data science technologies and the growing demand for real-time applications, streaming data has assumed an increasingly prominent role in modern data processing systems, continuously challenging traditional batch-processing paradigms. To address key challenges in streaming learning—such as extreme class imbalance, concept drift, and the requirement for millisecond-level latency response—this paper proposes STRAP (Streaming Temporal deep learning with Robust Attentive Prediction), an end-to-end deep streaming prediction framework. STRAP constructs temporal inputs using a sliding-window mechanism combined with causal slicing, ensuring predictions rely solely on current and historical information. For representation learning, it integrates bidirectional gated recurrent units (BiGRUs) with a multi-head attention mechanism to capture complex contextual dependencies. Furthermore, Focal Loss is incorporated to dynamically adjust class weights, thereby enhancing the model’s ability to learn from minority classes. Recognizing the lack of standardized evaluation protocols in streaming learning, this paper introduce WASE (Window- Adaptive Streaming Evaluation), a comprehensive assessment framework that jointly evaluates deployment performance along both accuracy and efficiency dimensions. WASE combines online AUC, latency percentiles (p95, p99), and system throughput, featuring a window-level adaptive evaluation mechanism that aligns with evolving data distributions and real-time operational requirements. In experiments on a streaming-reconstructed version of the IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection dataset, STRAP achieves a 1.5% absolute improvement in test-set AUC over an MLP baseline while maintaining a p99 latency below 7 ms, and attains a throughput of 1,258.2 samples/s. Ablation studies confirm that the multi-head attention mechanism and the dynamic reweighting strategy jointly improve minority-class recognition. These results demonstrate that STRAP delivers both high predictive accuracy and ultra-low-latency responsiveness in highly dynamic, high-concurrency streaming environments, exhibiting strong practical deployability for latency-sensitive real-time forecasting scenarios such as smart grid anomaly detection, financial risk control, and edge-based monitoring systems.

title: Designing Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Models: A Unified Path-Space View
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training provides a direct way to align diffusion models with human preferences and task-specific rewards. However, current RL algorithms for diffusion models remain fragmented: reverse-trajectory methods rely on discretized likelihood ratios, whereas forward-matching methods train on reward-labeled noising versions of the rollout samples. This paper shows that these seemingly different losses arise from a single path-space principle. Starting from the regularized diffusion-RL objective, we use importance sampling between sampling SDEs to obtain an explicit policy-gradient estimator on trajectory space. The estimator contains the stochastic Itô integral underlying Flow-GRPO-type updates; we derive an equivalent variance-reduced value-gradient form that recovers the forward-matching structure of AWM and DiffusionNFT. This identifies the empirical gap between these method families as a variance-reduction effect rather than a difference in RL principle. The derivation yields a unified design space organized by value-gradient estimation, weight functions, and sampling choices. Within this space, we propose a multi-sample KDE value-gradient estimator that reuses rollout groups, together with scale-bounded weight families that retain stable existing recipes while excluding singular ones. Experiments on SD3.5-M and Qwen-Image models validate the variance-reduction explanation and show that the resulting recipe improves over prior diffusion-RL baselines.

This identifies the empirical gap between these method families as a variance-reduction effect rather than a difference in RL principle. The derivation yields a unified design space organized by value-gradient estimation, weight functions, and sampling choices. Within this space, we propose a multi-sample KDE value-gradient estimator that reuses rollout groups, together with scale-bounded weight families that retain stable existing recipes while excluding singular ones. Experiments on SD3.5-M and Qwen-Image models validate the variance-reduction explanation and show that the resulting recipe improves over prior diffusion-RL baselines.

title: Multi-quantum-channel mediated tunable single-photon skyrmions from metasurfaces
abstract: Quantum optical skyrmions, as topologically robust quantum information carriers, hold transformative potential for resilient high-dimensional quantum information networks. However, their practical exploitation was still restricted to a single quantum channel, which precludes the multiplexing essential for practical high-capacity quantum networks. Here, we utilize a metasurface to achieve multi-channel quantum state distribution of the polarization-entangled photon pairs, inducing a two-photon bunching effect in both the spin and spatial dimensions with compact flat optics. At the spatial bunching port, controlled manipulation of the spin-orbit interaction enables the generation of a tunable single-photon skyrmion pair. In contrast to any prior skyrmion generation, the single-photon skyrmions are mediated and topologically controlled by quantum measurement in multiple channels. Concurrently, during the amplitude and phase modulation process, both the skyrmion localization and the texture helicity can be precisely customized. The proposed tunable single-photon skyromions offer multidimensional controllability and topological stability provide a viable path toward noise-resilient high-dimensional quantum information processing.

title: Musical Mirrors: The LLM as Sounding Board in Songwriting
abstract: This paper examines a use of AI in creative practice as an interpretive sounding board for human-generated material, rather than the more familiar pattern of AI generation followed by human curation. Through the lens of resonance as theorized by Hartmut Rosa, I present a first-person case study of songwriting from July 2025 to March 2026, drawing on 16 original pieces in English, French, and other languages along with piano solos. I describe a configuration in which resonance is not located between user and model, but in the author's deepening contact with their own material, mediated through the model. This kind of resonance was supported rather than inhibited by AI when sounding-board behavior was cultivated through sustained calibration by the user. Two failure modes appeared when calibration was absent: sycophantic drift and magical overinterpretation. This account suggests both the potential and the risks of AI as an interpretive partner in creative practice.

title: AdvDex: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Human Demonstrations via Joint-Aligned Actions and Adversarial Learning
abstract: Dexterous manipulation is a fundamental capability for embodied intelligence, but scaling it remains difficult because robot demonstrations are expensive to collect and action spaces vary across embodiments. Policies trained on heterogeneous data can also entangle task-relevant visual cues with embodiment-specific appearance, limiting cross-embodiment generalization. We present AdvDex, a unified Vision-Language-Action framework for learning dexterous manipulation from human and robot demonstrations. First, we introduce OmniShare, a large-scale multimodal dataset of human manipulation demonstrations that provides high-quality kinematic supervision and tactile measurements while reducing reliance on robot teleoperation. Second, we propose the Joint-Aligned Action Space (JAAS), a canonical action representation comprising an $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ wrist pose and 15 finger joints, thereby functionally aligning human hands, dexterous robot hands, and parallel grippers. Finally, we use domain-adversarial learning to reduce embodiment-specific information in the learned visual representation. Experiments on hand-action prediction and real-world dexterous manipulation show consistent improvements over baselines, effective zero-shot human-to-robot skill transfer, generalization to unseen objects and environments, and data-efficient few-shot adaptation.

title: On the Effect of Bit-Level Parameter Perturbations in Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models
abstract: In this chapter, we investigate how classical machine learning models respond to small, targeted modifications in their parameters. We compare and contrast these results to analogous experiments on deep learning models. For classical learning models, we consider Hidden Markov Models (HMM) and Support Vector Machines (SVM), and for comparison, we conduct analogous experiments involving Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. When applied to the Drebin Android malware dataset, our results show that classical models are brittle, in the sense that a limited set of selected parameters can have a dramatic effect on model behavior. In a related set of experiments, we investigate the steganographic capacity of these same learning models, that is, the proportion of bits in model parameters that can be overwritten without having a significant adverse affect on a model. We find that classical models offer limited steganographic capacity due to their compact, parameter-efficient, and relatively sensitive parameter structure. In contrast, neural networks are parameter-redundant, enabling higher steganographic capacity, where modifications can be distributed across many parameters with minimal impact on performance. These results highlight differences in how classical and neural models respond to parameter changes, with clear implications for both robustness and hidden information embedding. Overall, this work provides a framework for understanding parameter sensitivity and steganographic capacity across different classes of learning models.

title: DETEKSI ANOMALI PROFIL KARYAWAN BERBASIS ATRIBUT HR MENGGUNAKAN ISOLATION FOREST DENGAN INTERPRETASI XGBOOST-SHAP PADA DASHBOARD MONITORING HR
abstract: Pemanfaatan Human Resources Analytics memungkinkan organisasi mengolah data karyawan secara lebih terstruktur untuk mendukung pemantauan dan pengambilan keputusan. Kebutuhan pemantauan menjadi penting ketika profil karyawan terbentuk dari kombinasi berbagai atribut, tetapi tidak memiliki label yang menunjukkan profil normal atau anomali. Penelitian pada bidang HR masih banyak berfokus pada prediksi attrition berbasis label, sedangkan deteksi ketidaklaziman multivariat yang dapat dijelaskan dan disajikan kepada pengguna masih terbatas. Penelitian ini mengembangkan alur kerja deteksi anomali menggunakan Isolation Forest, XGBoost sebagai model pengganti, SHAP sebagai metode interpretasi, dan dashboard pemantauan HR sebagai media penyajian. Himpunan data IBM HR Analytics Employee Attrition & Performance yang terdiri atas 1.470 profil diproses melalui seleksi atribut, standardisasi fitur numerik, dan pengodean satu-panas sehingga menghasilkan 44 fitur. Isolation Forest menghasilkan skor ketidaklaziman yang dikelompokkan menggunakan ambang P90 dan P95 menjadi 1.323 profil kategori rendah, 73 kategori sedang, dan 74 kategori tinggi. Evaluasi terhadap 30 nilai acak menghasilkan median korelasi Spearman sebesar 0,9472. XGBoost memperoleh R² data uji sebesar 0,9022, sedangkan 30 kali Monte Carlo Cross-Validation menghasilkan median Spearman sebesar 0,9565 dan rata-rata kesamaan lima fitur SHAP teratas sebesar 0,8864. Seluruh sepuluh skenario pengujian kotak hitam berhasil, validasi ahli materi memperoleh nilai 68% dengan kategori layak, dan evaluasi ahli media menghasilkan skor System Usability Scale sebesar 85 dengan interpretasi Excellent. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa alur kerja menghasilkan peringkat profil yang relatif konsisten, model pengganti dengan fidelitas kuat, dan dashboard yang layak digunakan sebagai alat bantu pemantauan awal. Hasil tersebut tidak membuktikan kebenaran substantif anomali dan tetap memerlukan peninjauan manusia karena acuan kebenaran anomali tidak tersedia...................The use of Human Resources Analytics enables organizations to process employee data more systematically to support monitoring and decision-making. Monitoring becomes important when employee profiles are formed from combinations of multiple attributes, while no labels are available to indicate whether a profile is normal or anomalous. Research in the HR domain remains largely focused on label-based attrition prediction, whereas explainable multivariate anomaly detection presented through a user-oriented system is still limited. This study developed an anomaly detection pipeline using Isolation Forest, XGBoost as a surrogate model, SHAP as an interpretation method, and an HR monitoring dashboard as the presentation medium. The IBM HR Analytics Employee Attrition & Performance dataset, consisting of 1,470 employee profiles, was processed through attribute selection, numerical feature standardization, and one-hot encoding, resulting in 44 features. Isolation Forest generated unusualness scores that were grouped using the P90 and P95 thresholds into 1,323 low-priority profiles, 73 medium-priority profiles, and 74 high-priority profiles. Evaluation across 30 random states produced a median Spearman correlation of 0.9472. XGBoost achieved a test R² of 0.9022, while 30 runs of Monte Carlo Cross-Validation produced a median Spearman correlation of 0.9565 and a mean top-five SHAP feature overlap of 0.8864. All ten black-box testing scenarios were successfully completed, material expert validation obtained a score of 68% and was categorized as feasible, and media expert evaluation produced a System Usability Scale score of 85, interpreted as Excellent. The results indicate that the pipeline generates relatively consistent profile rankings, a surrogate model with strong fidelity, and a dashboard suitable for initial monitoring support. These findings do not establish the substantive validity of the detected anomalies and still require human review because anomaly ground truth is unavailable.
